tools.name: visa_salary_check
tools.description: Checks whether a salary meets the 2026 IND salary requirement for a Dutch highly skilled migrant (kennismigrant) permit or an EU Blue Card. Holiday allowance does not count; a 13th month counts only when paid monthly. Also checks the 30% ruling salary norm.

tools.name: job_loss_planner

tools.name: dutch_tax_changes_2027
tools.description: Compares income tax on a gross salary in 2026 with the Belastingplan 2027 proposal (presented on Prinsjesdag 2026, a proposal until Parliament votes): brackets and tax credits, and the 30% ruling dropping to 27% unless it started before 2024.

tools.name: transfer_tax_netherlands
tools.description: Overdrachtsbelasting in 2026 when buying a home in the Netherlands: 2% for a home you live in, 0% for first-time buyers aged 18-34 up to a €555,000 price, 8% for other homes.

tools.name: thirty_percent_ruling_timeline
tools.description: Net income year by year for an employee with the Dutch 30% ruling: 30%, then 27% from 2027 for rulings that started in 2024 or later, the salary norm, the end of the ruling after five years, and Box 3 on Dutch and foreign assets (partial non-resident status only for rulings that started before 2024)

tools.name: rent_vs_buy_netherlands
tools.description: Compares the net cost of renting and of buying a home in the Netherlands over a number of years: rent with yearly increases and the return on the down payment if it stays invested (after Box 3), against mortgage payments, maintenance, the mortgage interest deduction and the equity built up.

tools.description: Inheritance tax in the Netherlands for 2026 for one heir: the exemption for a partner, child, disabled child, grandchild, parent or anyone else, and the rates of each group. Due when the deceased lived in the Netherlands.

tools.name: company_car_tax_netherlands
tools.description: The yearly addition to income (bijtelling) for private use of a company car in the Netherlands in 2026, for electric and fuel cars (with the 60-month lock-in of an electric car's rate and cap from its first registration), and the extra income tax at the employee's marginal rate.

tools.name: pension_annuity_room_jaarruimte
tools.description: How much an employee or freelancer in the Netherlands may deposit into an annuity (lijfrente) or pension bank account in 2026 and deduct in Box 1: the jaarruimte from last year's income and factor A, unused room from earlier years (reserveringsruimte), and the tax the remaining room saves.

tools.description: The hourly rate a freelancer (ZZP) in the Netherlands needs in 2026 to take home a target net amount a month, after holidays, sick days and hours that can't be invoiced, business costs, the entrepreneur deductions, income tax and the Zvw contribution.

tools.name: rsu_tax_netherlands
tools.description: Tax on restricted stock units in the Netherlands: each vest is taxed as wages in Box 1 at the value on the vesting day (with or without the 30% ruling), and shares you keep fall into Box 3 the next year. Year by year, with sell-to-cover or keeping the shares.

tools.name: arrival_departure_year_m_form
tools.description: For the year someone arrives in or leaves the Netherlands (the M-form, migration tax return): the salary earned while resident, the Dutch tax on it with the tax credits for that part of the year, and the net pay a month during the resident period.

tools.description: The yearly cost of basic health insurance in the Netherlands in 2026: premium (with the discount for a voluntary extra deductible), the deductible (eigen risico) actually paid for expected care costs, and the healthcare allowance (zorgtoeslag) for the income.

tools.name: aow_state_pension
tools.description: The Dutch state pension (AOW) from 1 July 2026 for a single person or someone with a partner: 2% of the full AOW for every insured year in the Netherlands in the 50 years before AOW age, gross and net a month, and the holiday allowance.

tools.description: The planned new Dutch Box 3 (Wet werkelijk rendement, from 2028): tax on the actual return of the year (interest, dividends, price changes of investments incl. unrealised, rental income, minus interest and costs), compared with today's notional system. A plan; details can still change.
